rows.label: Concept
rows.text: IUPAC replaced the tangled IA/VIIIB/zero labels with **consecutive group numbers 1–18** and gave every not-yet-named element a mechanical stand-in name: split the atomic number into digits, translate each through the roots nil-un-bi-tri-quad-pent-hex-sept-oct-enn, append **-ium**, and take the roots' initials as the symbol (Unnilquadium, Unq, for Z = 104; Ununoctium, Uuo, for Z = 118).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Name = root(Z₁) + root(Z₂) + root(Z₃) + ium - Symbol = first letter of each root (capital first letter only) - enn + nil → ennil (single n)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Unnilquadium vs unnilquadium:** the symbol Unq capitalises only its first letter; the name capitalises only its first letter too — "UNQ"/"UNNILQUADIUM" are wrong.  ·  **Z = 118 is Og, not Uuo, today:** the temporary name served 2002–2016; examiners accept either but the permanent name earns the mark.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The name of an element awaiting permanent ratification is built from the digits of its atomic number plus the suffix -ium."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Z = 104 → Un-nil-quad-ium → Unnilquadium (Unq)*** — the template derivation; repeat the same three steps for any Z.

rows.text: Covers only: iupac classification of elements (within Classification of Elements and Periodic Table).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Naming the Table's Empty Seats New superheavy elements spend years with only an atomic number and no agreed name. IUPAC's solution: a **systematic temporary name built from the digits of Z**, so every element — named or not — has an unambiguous label and a definite place in the table. The scheme also fixes the group-numbering system (1–18) that replaced the old IA/VIIIA maze.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 IUPAC group numbering (1–18) - The old split notation (IA, IIA, IIIB… VIIIB, zero group) is replaced by **consecutive numbering 1 to 18**. - Mapping: old IA → 1, IIA → 2, IIIB → 3 … VIIIB (iron family) → 8, 9, 10, IB → 11, IIB → 12, IIIA → 13 … VIIA → 17, zero → 18.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Digit chant: "nil-un-bi-tri-quad-pent-hex-sept-oct-enn." Symbol = initials in order. Only rule to memorise: enn + nil → ennil.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): State the IUPAC systematic nomenclature rules for elements with Z > 100 and derive the name for Z = 108.** — Rules: (1) split Z into digits and use the roots 0 nil, 1 un, 2 bi, 3 tri, 4 quad, 5 pent, 6 hex, 7 sept, 8 oct, 9 enn; (2) add the suffix **-ium**; (3) the symbol is formed from the roots' initials (first letter…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Write the temporary IUPAC name and symbol for Z = 111, and give its permanent name.** — 1, 1, 1 → un, un, un → **Unununium, Uuu**; permanent name **Roentgenium (Rg)**, honouring Röntgen.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Show the digit split (e.g. 117 → 1·1·7) before writing the name — the marker checks the working. Quote at least one permanent counterpart (Rf, Db, Og) for presentation credit.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Name = digits of Z:** the temporary name is a mechanical translation of the atomic number — no chemistry needed, so it works for elements not yet discovered.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: IUPAC groups: 1–18 consecutive (old IA→1 … zero→18). Temporary names for unnamed elements: digits → roots (0 nil, 1 un, 2 bi, 3 tri, 4 quad, 5 pent, 6 hex, 7 sept, 8 oct, 9 enn) + -ium; symbol = root initials. Special: enn+nil → ennil. Stock pairs: 104 Unq/Rf, 105 Unp/Db, 110 Uun/Ds, 111 Uuu/Rg, 118 Uuo/Og.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Oganesson (Og, Z = 118) honours Yuri Oganessian — only the second element named after a living scientist (after Seaborgium).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Convert the old notations IIA, VIIA and 0 into IUPAC group numbers.** — IIA → **group 2** (alkaline earths); VIIA → **group 17** (halogens); 0 → **group 18** (noble gases). IUPAC numbers the 18 columns consecutively.  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Apply the 'enn' rule: write the temporary name for Z = 190.** — 1, 9, 0 → un, enn, nil → the duplicate n is dropped before nil → **Unennilium**, symbol **Ueo**.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **IUPAC** | International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry — the naming authority | Ratifies element names | | **Systematic temporary name** | Digit-root name for an element awaiting confirmation | Unnilquadium for Z = 104 | | **Element 118 (Og)** | Oganesson — completes period 7 | Named…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Building a name — the 3m drill **Q: Derive the IUPAC temporary name and symbol for Z = 117.** Digits: 1, 1, 7 → un, un, sept → **Ununseptium**, symbol **Uus** (now permanently Tennessine, Ts). The method: split Z into digits, translate each to its root, append -ium, take initials for the symbol.…  ·  ## 5. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Symbol vs name initials:** the symbol comes from the **root initials in order** — Z = 107 → Un-nil-Septium → **Uus**; taking 'U' + element meaning loses the mark.  ·  **enn before nil vs before oct:** drop the duplicate n only before **nil** (ennil); before other roots and before -ium the full "enn" stays.  ·  **Temporary names never use capital roots:** Unnilquadium — only the first letter is capital; "unNilquadium" is wrong.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **NEB-style (2m): Write the IUPAC name and symbol for the element with Z = 121.** — Digits 1, 2, 1 → un, bi, un → **Unbiunium**, symbol **Ubu** (a hypothetical period-8 element).  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Why did IUPAC introduce systematic nomenclature?** — Rival discovery claims (Z = 104–109) created naming disputes; a rule-based name derived from Z is neutral and unambiguous until priority is settled and a permanent name ratified.  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Convert old group VIIA and group 0 to IUPAC numbering.** — VIIA → **group 17** (halogens); group 0 → **group 18** (noble gases).
